01
Before the first verse · Vol. 4, p. 615

Opening of the surah

Vol. 4, p. 615
Sūrat Nūḥ is Makkan, and has twenty-eight verses [revealed after al-Naḥl]. In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
سورة نوح مكية، وهي ثمان وعشرون آية [نزلت بعد النحل] بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 71:1–4 · Vol. 4, p. 615

Verses 1 to 4

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. 'Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], "Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment."' (1) 'He said, "O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner:"' (2) '"that you worship God, fear Him and obey me."' (3) '"He will forgive you of your sins and delay you to a specified term. Indeed, the term of God, when it comes, is not delayed, if you only knew."' (4)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ أَنْ أَنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ (1) قالَ يا قَوْمِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ (2) أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ (3) يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى إِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ إِذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (4)
Vol. 4, p. 615
'That you warn': its origin is "bi-an anḏhir", so the preposition was dropped and the verb made directly transitive; and it is "an" which governs the verb in the subjunctive. The meaning: We sent him by saying to him "warn", i.e. We sent him with the command to give notice. It is also possible that it is explanatory, because "sending" contains the sense of "saying". Ibn Masʿūd recited "anḏhir" without "an", on the intended sense of saying. And 'that you worship God' is like 'that you warn' in the two possible analyses.
أَنْ أَنْذِرْ أصله: بأن أنذر، فحذف الجار وأوصل الفعل: وهي أن الناصبة للفعل، والمعنى: أرسلناه بأن قلنا له أنذر، أى: أرسلناه بالأمر بالإنظار. ويجوز أن تكون مفسّرة، لأنّ الإرسال فيه معنى القول. وقرأ ابن مسعود: أنذر بغير «أن» على إرادة القول. وأَنِ اعْبُدُوا نحو أَنْ أَنْذِرْ في الوجهين.
Question
If you say: How did he say 'and He will delay you' while informing that the term cannot be delayed? Is this anything but a contradiction?
فإن قلت: كيف قال وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ مع إخباره بامتناع تأخير الأجل، وهل هذا إلا تناقض؟
Answer
I say: For example, God decreed that if the people of Noah believed, their lifespan would be a thousand years, and if they remained in their disbelief He would destroy them at the end of nine hundred; so it was said to them: Believe, and He will delay you 'to a specified term', i.e. to a time God named and set as a limit to which you will come to an end and not exceed, which is the longer time, the completion of the thousand. Then He informed that when that term, that limit, comes, it is not delayed as this time is delayed, and you will have no ruse; so hasten in the times of respite and delay.
قلت: قضى الله مثلا أنّ قوم نوح إن آمنوا عمرهم ألف سنة، وإن بقوا على كفرهم أهلكهم على رأس تسعمائة، فقيل لهم: آمنوا يؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى، أى: إلى وقت سماه الله وضربه أمدا تنتهون إليه لا تتجاوزونه، وهو الوقت الأطول تمام الألف. ثم أخبر أنه إذا جاء ذلك الأجل الأمد لا يؤخر كما يؤخر هذا الوقت، ولم تكن لكم حيلة، فبادروا في أوقات الإمهال والتأخير.
03
Q 71:5–20 · Vol. 4, pp. 615–619

Verses 5 to 20

The verses as the commentary quotes them
'He said, "My Lord, indeed I invited my people night and day,"' (5) '"but my invitation increased them not except in flight."' (6) '"And indeed, every time I invited them that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their garments and persisted and were arrogant with [great] arrogance."' (7) '"Then I invited them publicly."' (8) '"Then I announced to them and confided to them secretly,"' (9) '"and said, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord; indeed, He is ever a Forgiver."' (10) '"He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in abundance"' (11) '"and give you increase in wealth and children and provide for you gardens and provide for you rivers."' (12) '"What is [wrong] with you that you do not attribute to God any dignity?"' (13) '"While He has created you in stages?"' (14) '"Do you not see how God has created seven heavens in layers"' (15) '"and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp?"' (16) '"And God has caused you to grow from the earth a [progressive] growth;"' (17) '"then He will return you into it and extract you [once more] in extraction."' (18) '"And God has made for you the earth an expanse"' (19) '"that you may follow therein roads of passage."' (20)
قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِي لَيْلاً وَنَهاراً (5) فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعائِي إِلاَّ فِراراً (6) وَإِنِّي كُلَّما دَعَوْتُهُمْ لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ جَعَلُوا أَصابِعَهُمْ فِي آذانِهِمْ وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ وَأَصَرُّوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا اسْتِكْباراً (7) ثُمَّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهاراً (8) ثُمَّ إِنِّي أَعْلَنْتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْراراً (9) فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً (10) يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْراراً (11) وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ أَنْهاراً (12) ما لَكُمْ لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقاراً (13) وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْواراً (14) أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقاً (15) وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُوراً وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِراجاً (16) وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَباتاً (17) ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيها وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْراجاً (18) وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ بِساطاً (19) لِتَسْلُكُوا مِنْها سُبُلاً فِجاجاً (20)
Vol. 4, p. 616
'Night and day' means continuously, without remission, taking up all times with it. 'But my invitation increased them not' makes the invitation the agent of the increase in flight. The meaning is that they increased in flight at it, because it is the cause of the increase. Similar are 'it increased them in filth upon their filth' and 'it increased them in faith'. 'That You might forgive them' means that they repent from their disbelief so that You forgive them; so He mentioned the thing caused, which is purely their benefit, to make their turning away from it uglier. They blocked their hearing against listening to the call. 'And covered themselves with their garments' and wrapped themselves in them, as though they sought that their garments cover them, or cover them over so as not to see him, out of dislike of looking at the face of one who counsels them concerning God's religion. It was also said: so that he would not recognize them, and this is supported by His saying 'Unquestionably, they fold up their breasts to hide from Him; unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments…'. "Al-iṣrār" is from "aṣarra al-ḥimār ʿalā al-ʿāna" «1», when it pricks its ears and turns to the herd, biting and driving it away: it was borrowed for turning to acts of disobedience and devoting oneself to them. 'And were arrogant': pride seized them away from «2» following Noah and obeying him; and the mention of the verbal noun is emphasis and an indication of the excess of their facing (him) and their insolence.
لَيْلًا وَنَهاراً دائبا من غير فتور مستغرقا به الأوقات كلها فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعائِي جعل الدعاء فاعل زيادة الفرار. والمعنى على أنهم ازدادوا عنده فرارا، لأنه سبب الزيادة. ونحوه فَزادَتْهُمْ رِجْساً إِلَى رِجْسِهِمْ، فَزادَتْهُمْ إِيماناً لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ ليتوبوا عن كفرهم فتغفر لهم، فذكر المسبب الذي هو حظهم خالصا ليكون أقبح لإعراضهم عنه. سدّوا مسامعهم عن استماع الدعوة وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ وتغطوا بها، كأنهم طلبوا أن تغشاهم ثيابهم، أو تغشيهم لئلا يبصروه كراهة النظر إلى وجه من ينصحهم في دين الله. وقيل: لئلا يعرفهم، ويعضده قوله تعالى أَلا إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ لِيَسْتَخْفُوا مِنْهُ أَلا حِينَ يَسْتَغْشُونَ ثِيابَهُمْ. الإصرار: من أصر الحمار على العانة «1» إذا صرّ أذنيه وأقبل عليها يكدمها ويطردها: استعير للإقبال على المعاصي والإكباب عليها وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا وأخذتهم العزة من «2» اتباع نوح وطاعته، وذكر المصدر تأكيد ودلالة على فرط استقبالهم وعتوهم.
Question
If you say: He mentioned that he invited them night and day, then invited them publicly, then invited them in secret and in the open; so they must be three different invitations for the coordination to be sound.
فإن قلت: ذكر أنه دعاهم ليلا ونهارا، ثم دعاهم جهارا، ثم دعاهم في السرو العلن، فيجب أن تكون ثلاث دعوات مختلفات حتى يصح العطف.
Answer
I say: He ﷺ did as one does who enjoins the right and forbids the wrong: beginning with the easier and ascending to the harder and harder; so he began with counsel in secret; and when they did not accept, he followed with public declaration; and when that had no effect, he made it a third by combining secrecy and publicity. The meaning of 'then' is to indicate the distance between states, because public is harsher than secret, and combining the two matters is harsher than singling out either. And 'publicly'
قلت: قد فعل عليه الصلاة والسلام كما يفعل الذي يأمر بالمعروف وينهى عن المنكر: في الابتداء بالأهون والترقي في الأشد فالأشد، فافتتح بالمناصحة في السر، فلما لم يقبلوا ثنى بالمجاهرة، فلما لم تؤثر ثلث بالجمع بين الإسرار والإعلان. ومعنى ثُمَّ الدلالة على تباعد الأحوال، لأن الجهار أغلظ من الإسرار، والجمع بين الأمرين، أغلظ من إفراد أحدهما. وجِهاراً
Vol. 4, p. 617
is in the accusative governed by "I invited them", the accusative of the verbal noun, because "invitation" has "jihār" as one of its two kinds, so it is put in the accusative by it as "al-qurfuṣāʾ" is by "qaʿada", since it is one of the kinds of sitting; or because he meant by "I invited them" "I made it public to them". It is also possible that it is an adjective of the verbal noun of "daʿā", in the sense of "an invitation publicly", i.e. made public; or a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial, i.e. "making it public". He commanded them to seek forgiveness, which is repentance from disbelief and acts of disobedience, and He offered them the promise of what is more effective in their souls and dearer to them: present benefits and immediate gains, as encouragement toward faith and its blessings and obedience and its results of good in both abodes, as He said 'and another [favor] which you love: help from God', 'and if only the people of the towns had believed and feared God, We would have opened upon them blessings', 'and if only they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them', and 'if they had remained straight upon the path, We would have given them to drink'. It was also said: when they denied him after long repetition of the call, God withheld rain from them and made the wombs of their women barren for forty years; it is also related: seventy. So he promised them that if they believed, God, the Exalted, would provide them with abundance and remove what they were in. And from ʿUmar ؓ: he went out to pray for rain and added nothing to seeking forgiveness. It was said to him: "We did not see you pray for rain!" He said: "I prayed for rain with the 'majādīḥ' of the sky, by which rain is brought down" «1». He likened seeking forgiveness to the truthful stars (anwāʾ) which do not fail. And from al-Ḥasan: a man complained to him of drought, so he said: "Seek God's forgiveness"; another complained to him of poverty, another of fewness of offspring, another of the poor yield of his land, and he commanded all of them to seek forgiveness. Al-Rabīʿ b. Ṣubayḥ said to him: "Men came to you complaining of different things and asking for different things, and you commanded all of them to seek forgiveness!" So he recited to him this verse. "Al-samāʾ" is the canopy, since the rain comes down from it to the clouds; it may also mean the clouds or the rain, as in his saying: "When the sky has descended upon a people's land" «2». And "al-midrār" is that which pours abundantly, and "mifʿāl" is among the forms in which masculine and feminine are alike, as they say: "a man or a woman miʿṭār and mitfāl". 'Gardens' means orchards. 'That you do not hope for any dignity from God' means you do not expect reverence, that is, magnification. The meaning: What is wrong with you that you are not in a state in which you hope for God's honoring you in the abode of reward «3»; 'for God' is an explanation of the one revered,
منصوب بدعوتهم، نصب المصدر لأنّ الدعاء أحد نوعيه الجهار، فنصب به نصب القرفصاء بقعد، لكونها أحد أنواع القعود. أو لأنه أراد بدعوتهم جاهرتهم. ويجوز أن يكون صفة لمصدر دعا، بمعنى دعاء جهارا، أى: مجاهرا به. أو مصدرا في موضع الحال، أى: مجاهرا. أمرهم بالاستغفار الذي هو التوبة عن الكفر والمعاصي، وقدّم إليهم الموعد بما هو أوقع في نفوسهم وأحبّ إليهم من المنافع الحاضرة والفوائد العاجلة، ترغيبا في الإيمان وبركاته والطاعة ونتائجها من خير الدارين، كما قال وَأُخْرى تُحِبُّونَها نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ، وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْقُرى آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكاتٍ، وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ، وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ لَأَسْقَيْناهُمْ وقيل: لما كذبوه بعد طول تكرير الدعوة: حبس الله عنهم القطر وأعقم أرحام نسائهم أربعين سنة. وروى: سبعين. فوعدهم أنهم إن آمنوا رزقهم الله تعالى الخصب ودفع عنهم ما كانوا فيه. وعن عمر رضى الله عنه: أنه خرج يستسقى، فما زاد على الاستغفار، فقيل له: ما رأيناك استسقيت! فقال: لقد استسقيت بمجاديح السماء التي يستنزل بها القطر «1» . شبه الاستغفار بالأنواء الصادقة التي لا تخطئ. وعن الحسن: أنّ رجلا شكا إليه الجدب فقال. استغفر الله، وشكا إليه آخر الفقر، وآخر قلة النسل، وآخر قلة ريع أرضه، فأمرهم كلهم بالاستغفار، فقال له الربيع بن صبيح: أتاك رجال يشكون أبوابا ويسألون أنواعا، فأمرتهم كلهم بالاستغفار! فتلا له هذه الآية. والسماء: المظلة لأنّ المطر منها ينزل إلى السحاب، ويجوز أن يراد السحاب أو المطر، من قوله. إذا نزل السّماء بأرض قوم «2» والمدرار: الكثير الدرور، ومفعال مما يستوي فيه المذكر والمؤنث، كقولهم: رجل أو امرأة معطار ومتفال جَنَّاتٍ بساتين لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقاراً لا تأملون له توقيرا أى تعظيما. والمعنى ما لكم لا تكونون على حال تأملون فيها تعظيم الله إياكم في دار الثواب «3» ، لِلَّهِ بيان للموقر،
Vol. 4, p. 618
and had it been delayed it would have been a complement to "dignity". And His saying 'while He has created you in stages' is in the position of a circumstantial clause, as though He said: "What is wrong with you that you do not believe in God, this being the case"—and it is a state that necessitates believing in Him—"because He created you in stages", i.e. at different times: He created you first from dust, then created you as sperm-drops, then created you as a clot, then created you as a lump, then created you as bones and flesh, then brought you forth as another creation. Or: do you not fear for God's forbearance and His leaving punishment un-hastened, so you believe? It was also said: What is wrong with you that you do not fear God's majesty? And from Ibn ʿAbbās: you do not fear the consequence from God, because the consequence is the state in which matters settle and reward and punishment are fixed, from "waqara" when it is firm and settled. He drew their attention first to looking into themselves, because they are the nearest thing for them to look at, then to looking at the world and what He fashioned in it of wonders that testify to the Maker whose power and knowledge are dazzling: the heavens and the earth, the sun and the moon. 'Therein' means in the heavens, though it is in the lowest heaven, because there is a connection among the heavens in that they are layered «1», so it is permissible to say "in them is such-and-such" even if it is not in all of them, as one says "in the city is such-and-such" while it is in some of its quarters. And from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar ؓ both: that the faces of the sun and the moon are toward the heaven and their backs toward the earth «2». 'And made the sun a lamp': the people of the world see in its light as the people of a house see in the light of a lamp what they need to see; the moon is not like that, but is only a light that does not reach the strength of the sun's radiance. Similar is His saying 'It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light'; and "ḍiyāʾ" is stronger than "nūr". "Planting" (inbāt) is borrowed for creating, as one says "God has planted you for good", and this metaphor is the most indicative of origination «3», because if they are plants they are necessarily originated, with the originating of plants; hence the "ḥashwiyya" were called "al-nābita" and "al-nawābit", because their doctrine arose in Islam without their having any precedence in it «4». Similarly is their saying "so-and-so has appeared (najama)" of one of the renegades. The meaning: He made you grow so you grew as plants; or it is accusative with "He caused you to grow" because it includes the meaning "you grew". 'Then He will return you into it' buried, 'and extract you' on the Day of Resurrection, and He emphasized it with the verbal noun, as though He said "He will extract you truly and without fail". 'He made it an expanse': spread out, on which you turn about as a man turns about on his carpet. 'Roads of passage' means wide, spacious.
ولو تأخر لكان صلة للوقار. وقوله وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْواراً في موضع الحال، كأنه قال: ما لكم لا تؤمنون بالله والحال هذه وهي حال موجبة للإيمان به، لأنه خلقكم أطوارا: أى تارات: خلقكم أوّلا ترابا، ثم خلقكم نطفا، ثم خلقكم علقا، ثم خلقكم مضغا، ثم خلقكم عظاما ولحما، ثم أنشأكم خلقا آخر. أو لا تخافون لله حلما وترك معاجلة العقاب فتؤمنوا؟ وقيل: ما لكم لا تخافون لله عظمة؟ وعن ابن عباس: لا تخافون لله عاقبة، لأن العاقبة حال استقرار الأمور وثبات الثواب والعقاب، من «وقر» إذا ثبت واستقرّ. نبههم على النظر في أنفسهم أوّلا، لأنها أقرب منظور فيه منهم، ثم على النظر في العالم وما سوّى فيه من العجائب الشاهدة على الصانع الباهر قدرته وعلمه من السماوات والأرض والشمس والقمر فِيهِنَّ في السماوات، وهو في السماء الدنيا، لأنّ بين السماوات ملابسة من حيث أنها طباق «1» فجاز أن يقال: فيهنّ كذا، وإن لم يكن في جميعهنّ، كما يقال: في المدينة كذا وهو في بعض نواحيها. وعن ابن عباس وابن عمر رضى الله عنهما: أنّ الشمس والقمر وجوههما مما يلي السماء وظهورهما مما يلي الأرض «2» وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِراجاً يبصر أهل الدنيا في ضوئها كما يبصر أهل البيت في ضوء السراج ما يحتاجون إلى إبصاره، والقمر ليس كذلك، إنما هو نور لم يبلغ قوّة ضياء الشمس. ومثله قوله تعالى هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِياءً وَالْقَمَرَ نُوراً والضياء: أقوى من النور. استعير الإنبات للإنشاء، كما يقال: زرعك الله للخير، وكانت هذه الاستعارة أدلّ على الحدوث «3» ، لأنهم إذا كانوا نباتا كانوا محدثين لا محالة حدوث النبات: ومنه قيل للحشوية: النابتة والنوابت، لحدوث مذهبهم في الإسلام من غير أوّلية لهم فيه «4» . ومنه قولهم: نجم فلان لبعض المارقة. والمعنى: أنبتكم فنبتم نباتا. أو نصب بأنبتكم لتضمنه معنى نبتم ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيها مقبورين ثم يُخْرِجُكُمْ يوم القيامة، وأكده بالمصدر كأنه قال يخرجكم حقا ولا محالة. جعلها بساطا مبسوطة تتقلبون عليها كما يتقلب الرجل على بساطه فِجاجاً واسعة منفجة.
Vol. 4, p. 619
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 4, p. 616
1. (1) . His saying "from 'aṣarra al-ḥimār ʿalā al-ʿāna'": "al-ʿāna" is a herd of wild donkeys, and "al-kadm" is biting with the front of the mouth. Reported by al-Ṣiḥāḥ. And in it: "ṣarra al-faras udhunayhi" means he pressed them to his head; and when they do not make it (the verb) take an object they say "aṣarra al-faras" with the alif. End. i.e. when they do not make the verb transitive to an object. (ʿ)
2. . His saying "and pride seized them away from following Noah": perhaps the right reading is "ʿan" (for "min"). (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «من أصر الحمار على العانة» هي القطيع من حمر الوحش، والكدم: العض بأدنى الفم. أفاده الصحاح. وفيه: صر الفرس أذنيه ضمها إلى رأسه، فإذا لم يوقعوا قالوا: أصر الفرس بالألف اه، يعنى: إذا لم يجعلوا الفعل متعديا إلى مفعول. (ع)
2. . قوله «وأخذتهم العزة من اتباع نوح» لعله: عن. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 617
1. (1) . Extracted by ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Abī Shayba, al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ, al-Ṭabarī and others from the transmission of al-Shaʿbī: that ʿUmar … with this, and he added: then he recited 'Seek forgiveness of your Lord; indeed, He is ever a Forgiver'; its men are reliable, except that it is interrupted (munqaṭiʿ).
2. . "When the sky has descended upon a people's land // we grazed it, even if they were angry." "Al-samāʾ" is applied to the canopy, to the clouds, and to the rain as here, for what is in it of loftiness and elevation; and it is applied to plants figuratively, because rain is their cause, and for that reason he said "we grazed it"; so in the verse there is "istikhdām" (a pun in which one word is used in one sense and its pronoun in another), since he used "al-samāʾ" in one meaning and returned the pronoun to it in another. And "al-ghiḍāb" is the plural of "ghaḍbān" (angry), and the meaning: we are brave, unlike others.
3. . Maḥmūd (al-Zamakhsharī) said: "What is wrong with you that you are not in a state in which there is the magnification of God, the Exalted … etc." Aḥmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: This interpretation keeps hope (rajāʾ) in its proper sense … etc.
1. (1) . أخرجه عبد الرزاق وابن أبى شيبة والطبراني في الدعاء والطبري وغيرهم من رواية الشعبي: أن عمر
…. بهذا وزاد: ثم قرأ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً ورجاله ثقات، إلا أنه منقطع.
2. . إذا نزل السماء بأرض قوم
…. رعيناه وإن كانوا غضابا تطلق السماء على المظلة، وعلى السحاب، وعلى المطر كما هنا، لما فيه من السمو والارتفاع، وتطلق على النبات مجازا، لأن المطر سببه، فلذلك قال: رعيناه، ففي الكلام استخدام، حيث أطلق السماء بمعنى، وأعاد عليها الضمير بمعنى آخر، والغضاب: جمع غضبان والمعنى: أننا شجعان دون غيرنا.
3. . قال محمود: «ما لكم لا تكونون على حال يكون فيها تعظيم الله تعالى
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وهذا التفسير يبقى الرجاء على بابه الخ.
Vol. 4, p. 618
1. (1) . Maḥmūd (al-Zamakhsharī) said: "It is in the lowest heaven only because between the heavens and the lowest heaven there is a connection." Aḥmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: And one should take note of 'From both of them emerge pearls and coral'.
2. . The ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās is a halted (Companion) report. Ibn Mardawayh extracted it in (Sūrat) Yūnus from the transmission of Ḥammād b. Salama from ʿAlī b. Zayd from Yūsuf b. Mihrān from him with this, in the wording "and their napes toward the earth"; and al-Ḥākim narrated from it only the mention of the moon. And the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar ؓ both, is like it: ʿAbd al-Razzāq extracted it from Maʿmar from Qatāda, who said: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar said: and he mentioned it as a halted report. And al-Ṭabarī narrated it from the route of Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī from Qatāda from Shahr b. Hawshab from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar. "Note": In the original "Ibn ʿUmar" occurs corrupted; it is actually "ʿUmar" ؓ both.
3. . His saying "most indicative of origination": perhaps: "the most indicative proof of origination". (ʿ)
4. . His saying "without their having any precedence in it": if by "ḥashwiyya" he means the Ahl al-Sunna, then their precedence in their doctrine is the Book and the Sunna. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «وإنما هو في السماء الدنيا لأن بين السماوات وبين السماء الدنيا مناسبة» قال أحمد: ويلاحظ يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ.
2. . حديث ابن عباس موقوف، أخرجه ابن مردويه في يونس من رواية حماد بن سلمة عن على بن زيد عن يوسف بن مهران عنه بهذا. بلفظ «وأقفيتهما إلى الأرض» وروى الحاكم منه ذكر القمر حسب. وحديث ابن عمر رضى الله عنهما مثله» أخرجه عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن قتادة قال: قال عبد الله بن عمر: فذكره موقوفا. وروى الطبري من طريق هشام الدستوائى عن قتادة عن شهر بن حوشب عن عبد الله بن عمر. «تنبيه» وقع في الأصل ابن عمر مصحف. وإنما هو عمر ورضى الله عنهما.
3. . قوله «أدل على الحدوث» لعله: أدل دليل على الحدوث. (ع)
4. . قوله «من غير أولية لهم فيه» إن كان مراده بالحشوية أهل السنة، فأوليتهم في مذهبهم: الكتاب والسنة. (ع)
04
Q 71:21–24 · Vol. 4, pp. 619–620

Verses 21 to 24

The verses as the commentary quotes them
'Noah said, "My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed him whose wealth and children will not increase him except in loss."' (21) 'And they conspired a great conspiracy.' (22) 'And they said, "Do not leave your gods, and do not leave Wadd or Suwāʿ or Yaghūth and Yaʿūq and Nasr."' (23) 'And already they have misled many. And, [my Lord], do not increase the wrongdoers except in error.' (24)
قالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي وَاتَّبَعُوا مَنْ لَمْ يَزِدْهُ مالُهُ وَوَلَدُهُ إِلاَّ خَساراً (21) وَمَكَرُوا مَكْراً كُبَّاراً (22) وَقالُوا لا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَلا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلا سُواعاً وَلا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْراً (23) وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا كَثِيراً وَلا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلاَّ ضَلالاً (24)
Vol. 4, p. 619
'And they followed' their foremost leaders, the owners of wealth and children, and adopted what they prescribed for them of clinging to the worship of idols; and He made their wealth and their children, which increased them in nothing but standing and benefit in this world, an addition 'of loss' in the Hereafter, and He treated that as an inseparable attribute of theirs and a mark by which they are known, to verify it, to affirm it and to nullify anything else. It is also recited "wa-wuldihi" with ḍamma on the wāw and with kasra. 'And they conspired' is coordinated to "did not increase", and the pronoun was made plural though it refers to "man", because it is in the sense of plural; and the conspirators are the leaders. Their conspiring: their scheming in religion and their plotting against Noah, their inciting people to harm him, and their turning them away from inclining to him and listening to him; and their saying to them "do not leave your gods" in favor of worshiping the Lord of Noah. 'A great conspiracy' is recited lightened and heavy: "kubbār" is greater than "kabīr", and "kubbār" is greater than "kubār"; similar to "ṭuwāl" and "ṭuwwāl". 'Do not leave Wadd': it seems these named ones were their largest idols and the greatest in their view, so they singled them out after their saying 'do not leave your gods'. These idols passed from the people of Noah to the Arabs: Wadd belonged to Kalb, Suwāʿ to Hamdān, Yaghūth to Madhḥij, Yaʿūq to Murād, and Nasr to Ḥimyar; and for that reason the Arabs named "ʿAbd Wadd" and "ʿAbd Yaghūth". It was also said they are names of righteous men. It was also said: of the children of Ādam who died, so Iblīs said to those after them: "If you made images of them, you would look at them," and they did; and when those died he said to those after them: "They used to worship them," so they worshiped them. It was also said: Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwāʿ in the form of a woman, Yaghūth in the form of a lion, Yaʿūq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of a vulture. It is also recited "wuddan" with ḍamma on the wāw. And al-Aʿmash recited "wa lā yaghūthan wa yaʿūqan" with tanwīn, which is a problematic reading, because if the two are Arabic or foreign, they have two causes of diptotism: either definiteness and the verb pattern, or definiteness and foreignness; perhaps he intended harmony, so he made them declinable, as he found their sisters declinable—Wadd, Suwāʿ and Nasr—as "wa-ḍuḥāhā" is recited with imāla because it occurs with words inclined for harmony. 'And already they have misled' — the pronoun refers to the leaders. Its meaning: they had already misled many before these ones who are being advised to cling to the worship of idols; these are not the first they misled. Or: they have misled by their misleading many, meaning that among these misleaders there is a multitude. It is also possible that it refers to the idols, as in His saying 'Indeed, they have led many people astray'. If you say: To what is His saying
وَاتَّبَعُوا رؤسهم المقدمين أصحاب الأموال والأولاد، وارتسموا ما رسموا لهم من التمسك بعبادة الأصنام، وجعل أموالهم وأولادهم التي لم تزدهم إلا وجاهة ومنفعة في الدنيا زائدة خَساراً في الآخرة، وأجرى ذلك مجرى صفة لازمة لهم وسمة يعرفون بها، تحقيقا له وتثبيتا، وإبطالا لما سواه. وقرئ: وولده بضم الواو وكسرها وَمَكَرُوا معطوف على لم يزده، وجمع الضمير وهو راجع إلى من، لأنه في معنى الجمع والماكرون: هم الرؤساء. ومكرهم: احتيالهم في الدين وكيدهم لنوح، وتحريش الناس على أذاه، وصدّهم عن الميل إليه والاستماع منه. وقولهم لهم: لا تذرون آلهتكم إلى عبادة رب نوح مَكْراً كُبَّاراً قرئ بالتخفيف والتثقيل. والكبار: أكبر من الكبير. والكبار: أكبر من الكبار، ونحوه: طوال وطوّال وَلا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا كأن هذه المسميات كانت أكبر أصنامهم وأعظمها عندهم، فخصوها بعد قولهم لا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وقد انتقلت هذه الأصنام عن قوم نوح إلى العرب، فكان ودّ لكلب، وسواع لهمدان، ويغوث لمذحج، ويعوق لمراد، ونسر لحمير، ولذلك سمت العرب بعبد ودّ وعبد يغوث. وقيل هي أسماء رجال صالحين. وقيل: من أولاد آدم ماتوا، فقال إبليس لمن بعدهم: لو صورتم صورهم فكنتم تنظرون إليهم، ففعلوا، فلما مات أولئك قال لمن بعدهم: إنهم كانوا يعبدونهم، فعبدوهم. وقيل: كان ودّ على صورة رجل، وسواع على صورة امرأة، ويغوث على صورة أسد، ويعوق على صورة فرس، ونسر على صورة نسر. وقرئ: ودّا، بضم الواو. وقرأ الأعمش: ولا يغوثا ويعوقا، بالصرف، وهذه قراءة مشكلة، لأنهما إن كانا عربيين أو عجميين ففيهما سببا منع الصرف: إما التعريف ووزن الفعل، وإما التعريف والعجمة، ولعله قصد الازدواج فصرفهما، لمصادفته أخواتهما منصرفات ودا وسواعا ونسرا، كما قرئ: وضحاها بالإمالة، لوقوعه مع الممالات للازدواج وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا الضمير للرؤساء. ومعناه: وقد أضلوا كَثِيراً قبل هؤلاء الموصين بأن يتمسكوا بعبادة الأصنام ليسوا بأوّل من أضلوهم. أو وقد أضلوا بإضلالهم كثيرا، يعنى أنّ هؤلاء المضلين فيهم كثرة. ويجوز أن يكون للأصنام، كقوله تعالى إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ. فإن قلت: علام عطف قوله
Vol. 4, p. 620
'and do not increase the wrongdoers' coordinated? I say: To His saying 'My Lord, they have disobeyed me', by way of reporting Noah's speech ﷺ after "he said" and after the wāw that stands in for it; its meaning: he said "My Lord, they have disobeyed me", and he said "Do not increase the wrongdoers except in error"; that is, he said these two sayings, and they are in the accusative position, being the two objects of "he said", as you say "Zayd said: 'the call to prayer has been made'—'and pray in the mosque'", reporting his two sayings with one coordinated to the other.
وَلا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ؟ قلت: على قوله رَبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي على حكاية كلام نوح عليه السلام بعد قالَ وبعد الواو النائبة عنه: ومعناه: قال رب إنهم عصوني، وقال: لا تزد الظالمين إلا ضلالا، أى: قال هذين القولين وهما في محل النصب، لأنهما مفعولا «قال» كقولك: قال زيد نودي للصلاة وصل في المسجد، تحكى قوليه معطوفا أحدهما على صاحبه.
Question
If you say: How could he wish error for them and pray to God for its increase?
فإن قلت: كيف جاز أن يريد لهم الضلال ويدعو الله بزيادته؟
Answer
I say: What is meant by error is that they be abandoned «1» and denied graces «2», because of their firm resolve on disbelief and the despair of their believing; and that is good and fine, and it is permissible to pray for it—indeed, praying for the opposite would not be good. It is also possible that by "error" he means loss and destruction, because of His saying 'and do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction'.
قلت: المراد بالضلال: أن يخذلوا «1» ويمنعوا الألطاف «2» ، لتصميمهم على الكفر ووقوع اليأس من إيمانهم، وذلك حسن جميل يجوز الدعاء به، بل لا يحسن الدعاء بخلافه. ويجوز أن يريد بالضلال: الضياع والهلاك، لقوله تعالى وَلا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا تَباراً.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 620
1. (1) . His saying "that they be abandoned and denied": is built on the doctrine of the Muʿtazila that He, the Exalted, does not will evil and does not do it. The answer is that he prayed against them in this way only after God, the Exalted, informed him that they would not believe, when He said to him: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed." This is according to the doctrine of the Ahl al-Sunna, who permitted that He, the Exalted, does evil, such as creating error in the heart, because His act is never without wisdom. (ʿ) [.....]
2. . Maḥmūd (al-Zamakhsharī) said: "How could he wish error, and he answered that what is meant is the denial of graces." I say: This is according to his principle.
1. (1) . قوله «يخذلوا ويمنعوا مبنى على مذهب المعتزلة أنه تعالى لا يريد الشر ولا يفعله، وأجيب: بأنه إنما دعا عليهم بذلك بعد أن أعلمه الله تعالى أنهم لا يؤمنون، حيث قال له: إنه لن يؤمن من قومك إلا من قد آمن. وهذا على مذهب أهل السنة الذين أجازوا أنه تعالى يفعل الشر كخلق الضلال في القلب، لأن فعله لا يخلو عن حكمة. (ع) [.....]
2. . قال محمود: «كيف جاز أن يريد الضلال، وأجاب بأن المراد به منع الألطاف» قلت: هذا على قاعدته.
05
Q 71:25–27 · Vol. 4, pp. 620–621

Verses 25 to 27

The verses as the commentary quotes them
'Because of their sins they were drowned and made to enter a Fire; and they found not for themselves besides God any helpers.' (25) 'And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant."' (26) 'Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and not beget except [every] immoral disbeliever.' (27)
مِمَّا خَطِيئاتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا فَأُدْخِلُوا ناراً فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْصاراً (25) وَقالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ لا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ دَيَّاراً (26) إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا عِبادَكَ وَلا يَلِدُوا إِلاَّ فاجِراً كَفَّاراً (27)
Vol. 4, p. 620
The fronting of 'because of their sins' is to show that their drowning by the flood, and their being made to enter the Fire, was only on account of their sins, and this meaning is emphasized by the addition of "mā"; and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "min khaṭīʾātihim mā ughriqū", with the clause delayed. It suffices as a deterrent for the one who commits sins, for the disbelief of Noah's people was one of their sins, though the greatest of them. All their other sins were denounced against them as their disbelief was denounced, and no distinction was made between it and them in necessitating punishment, so that the sinning Muslim would not rely on his Islam but know that he has with him what necessitates punishment even if he is free of the greatest sin. It is also recited "khaṭīʾātihim" with hamza, "khaṭiyyātihim" with the hamza turned to yāʾ and assimilated, "khaṭāyāhum", and "khaṭīʾatihim" in the singular, intending the genus; and it is possible that disbelief is meant. 'And made to enter a Fire': He made their entering the Fire in the Hereafter as though it immediately follows their drowning, because of its nearness and because it is bound to happen, so it is as though it has already happened. Or the punishment of the grave is meant; for whoever dies in water or in fire or is eaten by beasts and birds, there befalls him what befalls the buried of punishment. And from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: they were drowned on one side and burned on another. The indefiniteness of "fire" is either for magnification or because God prepared for them, according to their sins, a kind of fire. 'And they found not for themselves besides God any helpers' is an allusion to their taking gods besides God, and that these are unable
تقديم مِمَّا خَطِيئاتِهِمْ لبيان أن لم يكن إغراقهم بالطوفان، فإدخالهم النار إلا من أجل خطيئاتهم، وأكد هذا المعنى بزيادة «ما» وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: من خطيئاتهم ما أغرقوا، بتأخير الصلة، وكفى بها مزجرة لمرتكب الخطايا، فإن كفر قوم نوح كان واحدة من خطيئاتهم، وإن كانت كبراهنّ. وقد نعيت عليهم سائر خطيئاتهم كما نعى عليهم كفرهم، ولم يفرق بينه وبينهن في استيجاب العذاب، لئلا يتكل المسلم الخاطئ على إسلامه، ويعلم أنّ معه ما يستوجب به العذاب وإن خلا من الخطيئة الكبرى. وقرئ: خطيئاتهم بالهمزة. وخطياتهم بقلبها ياء وإدغامها. وخطاياهم. وخطيئتهم. بالتوحيد على إرادة الجنس. ويجوز أن يراد الكفر فَأُدْخِلُوا ناراً جعل دخولهم النار في الآخرة كأنه متعقب لإغراقهم، لاقترابه، ولأنه كائن لا محالة، فكأنه قد كان. أو أريد عذاب القبر. ومن مات في ماء أو في نار أو أكلته السباع والطير: أصابه ما يصيب المقبور من العذاب. وعن الضحاك: كانوا يغرقون من جانب ويحرقون من جانب. وتنكير النار إما لتعظيمها، أو لأن الله أعد لهم على حسب خطيئاتهم نوعا من النار فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْصاراً تعريض باتخاذهم آلهة من دون الله وأنها غير قادرة
Vol. 4, p. 621
to help them, and a mockery of them, as though He said: "So they found no gods besides God to help them and protect them from God's punishment", as in His saying 'Or do they have gods that defend them besides Us?' 'An inhabitant' (dayyār) is among the nouns used in general negation: one says "there is no dayyār in the house", and "dayyūr", like "qayyām" and "qayyūm"; it is "fayʿāl" from "dawr" or from "dār", the original being "diwwār", to which was done what was done to the original of "sayyid" and "mayyit"; and if it were "faʿʿāl" it would be "dawwār".
على نصرهم، وتهكم بهم، كأنه قال: فلم يجدوا لهم من دون الله آلهة ينصرونهم ويمنعونهم من عذاب الله، كقوله تعالى أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنا. دَيَّاراً من الأسماء المستعملة في النفي العام، يقال: ما بالدار ديار وديور، كقيام وقيوم، وهو فيعال من الدور. أو من الدار، أصله ديوار، ففعل به ما فعل بأصل سيد وميت، ولو كان فعالا لكان دوّارا.
Question
If you say: How was it known that their children would disbelieve, and how did he describe them as disbelievers at birth?
فإن قلت: بم علم أن أولادهم يكفرون، وكيف وصفهم بالكفر عند الولادة؟
Answer
I say: He remained among them a thousand years less fifty, so he tasted them, tested them and knew their natures and conditions; and a man of them would take his son to him and say: "Beware of this one, for he is a liar, and my father warned me about him"; so the old would die and the young grow up on that. And God, Mighty and Majestic, had informed him that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed. And the meaning of 'and not beget except an immoral disbeliever' is that they do not beget except one who will become immoral and disbelieving. So He described them by what they will become, as in his saying ﷺ: "Whoever kills a slain one, his is the spoils" «1».
قلت: لبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما، فذاقهم وأكلهم وعرف طباعهم وأحوالهم، وكان الرجل منهم ينطلق بابنه إليه، ويقول: احذر هذا، فإنه كذاب، وإن أبى حذرنيه فيموت الكبير وينشأ الصغير على ذلك، وقد أخبره الله عز وجل أنه لن يؤمن من قومك إلا من قد آمن، ومعنى لا يَلِدُوا إِلَّا فاجِراً كَفَّاراً لا يلدوا إلا من سيفجر ويكفر. فوصفهم بما يصيرون إليه، كقوله عليه السلام «من قتل قتيلا فله سلبه» «1»
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 620
1. (1) . His saying "that they be abandoned and denied": is built on the doctrine of the Muʿtazila that He, the Exalted, does not will evil and does not do it. The answer is that he prayed against them in this way only after God, the Exalted, informed him that they would not believe, when He said to him: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed." This is according to the doctrine of the Ahl al-Sunna, who permitted that He, the Exalted, does evil, such as creating error in the heart, because His act is never without wisdom. (ʿ) [.....]
2. . Maḥmūd (al-Zamakhsharī) said: "How could he wish error, and he answered that what is meant is the denial of graces." I say: This is according to his principle.
1. (1) . قوله «يخذلوا ويمنعوا مبنى على مذهب المعتزلة أنه تعالى لا يريد الشر ولا يفعله، وأجيب: بأنه إنما دعا عليهم بذلك بعد أن أعلمه الله تعالى أنهم لا يؤمنون، حيث قال له: إنه لن يؤمن من قومك إلا من قد آمن. وهذا على مذهب أهل السنة الذين أجازوا أنه تعالى يفعل الشر كخلق الضلال في القلب، لأن فعله لا يخلو عن حكمة. (ع) [.....]
2. . قال محمود: «كيف جاز أن يريد الضلال، وأجاب بأن المراد به منع الألطاف» قلت: هذا على قاعدته.
Vol. 4, p. 621
1. (1) . Agreed upon (Bukhārī and Muslim), and it has been mentioned earlier.
2. . Maḥmūd (al-Zamakhsharī) said: "What necessitated their drowning when they were drowned? And he answered that they were not drowned by way of punishment … etc." Aḥmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: This question reveals what is within it of the necessity of giving causes for the acts of God, the Exalted, and on it is built the view that pain from God, the Exalted, is not permissible except through a prior desert, or for anticipated compensation, or for other benefits, based on their principle of the sound and the soundest; and the children had no prior offense nor compensation to be anticipated for them. So the question arises on that basis. As for the Ahl al-Sunna, God, the Exalted, has Himself undertaken the answer on their behalf with His saying 'He is not questioned about what He does.' And this speech concerns the particular case of Noah's people; and the discussion draws from it to God's ruling about us regarding the enemy: if it is feared that fighting them with weapons would harm their offspring, that does not necessitate refraining from fighting them with weapons that destroy and scatter them. It is argued from the Prophet's ﷺ hurling catapults at the people of al-Ṭāʾif. It was said to him that among them were offspring, so he said: "They are from their fathers." As for hurling fire at them when offspring are among them: Mālik ؒ forbade it, unless their treachery is feared, so they are hit with it if they are not repelled by other means. And God, the Exalted, knows best.
1. (1) . متفق عليه، وقد تقدم.
2. . قال محمود: «ما موجب إغراقهم حين أغرقوا، وأجاب بأنهم ما أغرقوا لا على وجه العقاب
…. الخ» قال أحمد: هذا السؤال مفصح عما في باطنه من وجوب تعليل أفعال الله تعالى، وعليه يبنى أنه لا يجوز الألم من الله تعالى إلا باستحقاق سابق، أو لأعواض مترقبة، أو لغير ذلك من المصالح، بناء على القاعدة لهم في الصلاح والأصلح والصبيان لا جناية سبقت منهم ولا عوض يترقب فيهم. فبرد السؤال على ذلك. وأما أهل السنة فالله تعالى قد تكفل الجواب عنهم بقوله لا يُسْئَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وهذا الكلام بالنظر إلى خصوص واقعة قوم نوح، وينجر الكلام منها إلى حكم الله علينا في العدو إذا خيف من مقاتلتهم بالآلات على ذراريهم أن ذلك لا يوجب الاكفاف عن مقاتلتهم بالآلات المهلكة لهم والمذرية، ويستدل برمي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على أهل الطائف بالمجانيق. وقيل له فيهم الذرية، فقال: هم من آبائهم، وأما رميهم بالنار وفيهم الذرية: فمنعه مالك رحمه الله، إلا أن يخاف غائلتهم فيرمون بها إن لم يندفعوا بغيرها، والله تعالى أعلم.
06
Q 71:28 · Vol. 4, pp. 621–622

Verse 28

The verse as the commentary quotes it
'My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house as a believer and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.' (28)
رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوالِدَيَّ وَلِمَنْ دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِناً وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ وَلا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلاَّ تَباراً (28)
Vol. 4, p. 621
'And my parents': his father was Lamk b. Mutawashshilkh, and his mother Shamkhā bt. Anūsh: they were believers. It was also said: they are Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ. Al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī recited "wa-li-waladayya", he means Sām and Ḥām. 'My house' means my home. It was also said: my mosque. It was also said: my ship. He singled out first those connected with him, because they are more deserving and have a greater right to his prayer, then extended it to the believing men and believing women. 'Destruction' (tabār) means perishing.
وَلِوالِدَيَّ أبوه لمك بن متوشلخ، وأمه شمخا بنت أنوش: كانا مؤمنين. وقيل. هما آدم وحواء. وقرأ الحسين بن على: ولولدي، يريد: ساما وحاما بَيْتِيَ منزلي. وقيل: مسجدى. وقيل: سفينتي، خص أوّلا من يتصل به، لأنهم أولى وأحق بدعائه، ثم عم المؤمنين والمؤمنات تَباراً هلاكا.
Question
If you say: What happened to their children when they were drowned?
فإن قلت: ما فعل صبيانهم حين أغرقوا؟
Answer
I say: They drowned with them, not by way of punishment «2», but as they die by various kinds of causes of death—how many of them die by drowning and burning—and it was as though that was an increase in the punishment of the fathers and mothers when they saw their infants drowning.
قلت: غرقوا معهم لا على وجه العقاب «2» ، ولكن كما يموتون بالأنواع من أسباب الموت، وكم منهم من يموت بالغرق والحرق، وكأن ذلك زيادة في عذاب الآباء والأمّهات إذا أبصروا أطفالهم يغرقون.
Vol. 4, p. 622
and from it is his saying ﷺ: "They are destroyed with one destruction and issue forth to various destinations" «1». And from al-Ḥasan: he was asked about that and said: God knew their innocence, so He destroyed them without punishment. It was also said: God made the wombs of their women barren and dried up the loins of their fathers before the flood by forty or seventy years, so there was no child among them when they were drowned. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Whoever recites Sūrat Nūḥ will be among the believers whom the supplication of Noah ﷺ reaches" «2».
ومنه قوله عليه السلام «يهلكون مهلكا واحدا ويصدرون مصادر شتى» «1» وعن الحسن: أنه سئل عن ذلك فقال: علم الله براءتهم فأهلكهم بغير عذاب. وقيل: أعقم الله أرحام نسائهم وأيبس أصلاب آبائهم قبل الطوفان بأربعين أو سبعين سنة، فلم يكن معهم صبى حين أغرقوا. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة نوح كان من المؤمنين الذين تدركهم دعوة نوح عليه السلام» «2» .
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 621
1. (1) . Agreed upon (Bukhārī and Muslim), and it has been mentioned earlier.
2. . Maḥmūd (al-Zamakhsharī) said: "What necessitated their drowning when they were drowned? And he answered that they were not drowned by way of punishment … etc." Aḥmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: This question reveals what is within it of the necessity of giving causes for the acts of God, the Exalted, and on it is built the view that pain from God, the Exalted, is not permissible except through a prior desert, or for anticipated compensation, or for other benefits, based on their principle of the sound and the soundest; and the children had no prior offense nor compensation to be anticipated for them. So the question arises on that basis. As for the Ahl al-Sunna, God, the Exalted, has Himself undertaken the answer on their behalf with His saying 'He is not questioned about what He does.' And this speech concerns the particular case of Noah's people; and the discussion draws from it to God's ruling about us regarding the enemy: if it is feared that fighting them with weapons would harm their offspring, that does not necessitate refraining from fighting them with weapons that destroy and scatter them. It is argued from the Prophet's ﷺ hurling catapults at the people of al-Ṭāʾif. It was said to him that among them were offspring, so he said: "They are from their fathers." As for hurling fire at them when offspring are among them: Mālik ؒ forbade it, unless their treachery is feared, so they are hit with it if they are not repelled by other means. And God, the Exalted, knows best.
1. (1) . متفق عليه، وقد تقدم.
2. . قال محمود: «ما موجب إغراقهم حين أغرقوا، وأجاب بأنهم ما أغرقوا لا على وجه العقاب
…. الخ» قال أحمد: هذا السؤال مفصح عما في باطنه من وجوب تعليل أفعال الله تعالى، وعليه يبنى أنه لا يجوز الألم من الله تعالى إلا باستحقاق سابق، أو لأعواض مترقبة، أو لغير ذلك من المصالح، بناء على القاعدة لهم في الصلاح والأصلح والصبيان لا جناية سبقت منهم ولا عوض يترقب فيهم. فبرد السؤال على ذلك. وأما أهل السنة فالله تعالى قد تكفل الجواب عنهم بقوله لا يُسْئَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وهذا الكلام بالنظر إلى خصوص واقعة قوم نوح، وينجر الكلام منها إلى حكم الله علينا في العدو إذا خيف من مقاتلتهم بالآلات على ذراريهم أن ذلك لا يوجب الاكفاف عن مقاتلتهم بالآلات المهلكة لهم والمذرية، ويستدل برمي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على أهل الطائف بالمجانيق. وقيل له فيهم الذرية، فقال: هم من آبائهم، وأما رميهم بالنار وفيهم الذرية: فمنعه مالك رحمه الله، إلا أن يخاف غائلتهم فيرمون بها إن لم يندفعوا بغيرها، والله تعالى أعلم.
Vol. 4, p. 622
1. (1) . Extracted by Muslim from the route of Ibn al-Zubayr from ʿĀʾisha ؓ.
2. . Extracted by al-Thaʿlabī, al-Wāḥidī and Ibn Mardawayh with their chains to Ubayy b. Kaʿb.
1. (1) . أخرجه مسلم من طريق ابن الزبير عن عائشة رضى الله عنها.
2. . أخرجه الثعلبي والواحدي وابن مردويه بأسانيدهم إلى أبى بن كعب.
